label: Early copy-phase steps (outputs 2-4) when the fed-back input is one of 3/e/t/c/u/x/o/v/j, in longer sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never on original tokens or on the <DEL> step. 95% of activation mass falls on recall_idx 1-3 (steps right after <DEL>, when the input is the fed-back original token 0-2), with recall_idx 2 strongest, and it is much more frequent in longer sequences (L>=6; essentially silent for L<=4). Within that window the input token identity strongly gates it: 3 and e have the highest rates, then t, c, u, x, o, v, j; tokens like h, d, f fire rarely. The largest activations are on input 3 at recall_idx 2 (i.e. orig(1)=3) in L=9 sequences. A weaker tail fires later in the copy phase, often on repeated tokens or after 3/e appeared, which the predicate misses. The token gating is graded rather than a clean set, so precision and recall both stay around 0.65-0.7.
